raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  build_number: 1
  name: opam
  version: "2.5.2"

  library: ${{ "Library/" if not unix else "" }}
  m2: ${{ "m2-" if not unix else "" }}
  sh: ${{ "sh" if unix else "bat" }}
  # ocaml_win-64 ships gcc_* and vs2022_* tracks; follow the c_compiler lane
  c_toolchain: ${{ "" if unix else c_compiler ~ "_*" }}

recipe:
  name: opam-packages
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/ocaml/${{ name }}/releases/download/${{ version }}/${{ name }}-full-${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: b3623809567f19ed6b5d679b8c7bbc0bdec9418bff4a875ff0799d446d8555c3
    target_directory: opam

build:
  number: ${{ build_number }}
  string: ${{ c_compiler ~ "_" if not unix else "" }}h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}
  dynamic_linking:
    missing_dso_allowlist:
      - if: not unix
        then:
          - C:/Windows/system32/SHLWAPI.dll
          - C:/Windows/system32/VERSION.dll

outputs:
  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}
      version: ${{ version }}
    build:
      # rattler-build 0.76 runs a bare "build.sh" as an inline command (exit 127)
      script:
        - if: unix
          then: bash "${RECIPE_DIR}/build.sh"
          else:
            - call "%RECIPE_DIR%\build.bat"
            - if errorlevel 1 exit 1
    requirements:
      build:
        - if: unix or arm64 or c_compiler == "vs2022"
          then:
            - ${{ compiler("c") }}
            - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
            - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
          else:
            - ${{ compiler("m2w64_c") }}
            - ${{ compiler("m2w64_cxx") }}
            - ${{ stdlib("m2w64_c") }}
        - ${{ m2 }}bash >=5.2
        - ${{ m2 }}bzip2
        - ${{ m2 }}findutils
        - ${{ m2 }}gawk
        - ${{ m2 }}grep
        - ${{ m2 }}make
        - ${{ m2 }}sed
        - ocaml-cppo
        - ocaml-dune
        - ocaml-menhir
        # no binutils package for win-arm64
        - if: not (win and arm64)
          then: binutils
        - curl
        - git
        - ${{ compiler("ocaml") }}
        # compiler() has no build string; pin the gcc/vs2022/zig track on Windows
        - if: not unix
          then: ocaml_${{ target_platform }} ${{ ocaml_compiler_version }}.* ${{ c_toolchain }}
        # the build_number>=18 floor (ocaml_use_cross/ocaml_use_native, standalone
        # cross ocaml) applies to cross lanes only
        # cross lanes build and run a native opam first (man pages, vendored parsers);
        # the cross compiler no longer pulls in the native one
        # build 18: cross toplevel can #load unix.cma, cross lib first on OCAMLPATH
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - ocaml_${{ build_platform }} ${{ ocaml_compiler_version }}.*[build_number=">=18"]
            - ocaml_${{ target_platform }} ${{ ocaml_compiler_version }}.*[build_number=">=18"]
        - if: build_platform != target_platform or target_platform == "win-arm64"
          then:
            - python >=3.9
        - if: unix
          then:
            # OCaml compiler has zstd paths embedded from its build environment.
            # We need zstd in build env so those paths resolve correctly.
            - file
            - unzip
            - zstd
          else:
            - ${{ m2 }}coreutils
            - ${{ m2 }}diffutils
            - ${{ m2 }}which
        - if: osx
          then:
            - lld
            - llvm-tools
      host:
        # the ocaml cross compiler links -lzstd into target executables (e.g.
        # dune's context_flags helpers); there is no zstd package for s390x
        - if: build_platform != target_platform and target_platform != "linux-s390x"
          then:
            - zstd
      ignore_run_exports:
        # opam itself does not link libzstd
        by_name:
          - zstd
      run:
        # c-compiler, curl, git, make, rsync are not yet built for linux-s390x
        - if: target_platform != "linux-s390x"
          then:
            - c-compiler
            - curl
            - git
            - if: unix
              then:
                - make
                - rsync
        # no unzip package for linux-riscv64 / linux-s390x
        - if: unix and not (target_platform == "linux-riscv64" or target_platform == "linux-s390x")
          then: unzip
        # no bubblewrap package for linux-s390x; opam sandboxing is optional
        - if: linux and target_platform != "linux-s390x"
          then:
            - bubblewrap
    tests:
      # Package contents validation (using brace expansion for conciseness)
      - package_contents:
          strict: true
          bin:
            - opam
            - opam-installer
          files:
            - ${{ library }}share/man/man1/opam*
            - etc/conda/activate.d/opam-activate.${{ sh }}
            - etc/conda/deactivate.d/opam-deactivate.${{ sh }}
            - ${{ library }}share/opam/conda/.opam-switch/{environment,lock,switch-config}
            - ${{ library }}share/opam/{config,config.lock,lock}
            - ${{ library }}share/opam/opam-init/complete.{sh,zsh}
            - ${{ library }}share/opam/opam-init/hooks/sandbox.{sh,sh.hash}
            - ${{ library }}share/opam/opam-init/init.{cmd,csh,fish,ps1,sh,zsh}
            - ${{ library }}share/opam/opam-init/variables.{cmd,csh,fish,ps1,sh}
            - ${{ library }}share/opam/repo/{default/repo,lock,repos-config}
            - etc/conda/test-files/*

      # Architecture verification - Unix only (uses otool/readelf)
      - if: unix
        then:
          script: bash testing/test-opam-arch.sh
          files:
            recipe:
              - testing/test-opam-arch.sh
          requirements:
            run:
              - if: linux
                then:
                  - binutils

      # Version check - native builds OR Linux cross-compile (QEMU/binfmt available)
      # macOS cross-compile: can't run ARM64 binaries, skip this test
      # no python for linux-s390x yet; package_contents and the arch check still run there
      - if: (build_platform == target_platform or linux) and target_platform != "linux-s390x"
        then:
          - script: |
              python testing/test-opam-version.py
            files:
              recipe:
                - testing/test-opam-version.py
            requirements:
              run:
                - python >=3.9
                - ocaml ${{ ocaml_compiler_version }}.*
                - if: not unix
                  then: ocaml_${{ target_platform }} ${{ ocaml_compiler_version }}.* ${{ c_toolchain }}

          # Functional tests - native builds OR Linux cross-compile
          # These run opam commands; Linux uses QEMU, macOS cross can't run ARM64
          - script: |
              python testing/test-opam-functional.py
              python testing/test-opam-activation.py
            files:
              recipe:
                - testing/test-opam-functional.py
                - testing/test-opam-activation.py
            requirements:
              run:
                - python >=3.9
                - ocaml ${{ ocaml_compiler_version }}.*
                - if: not unix
                  then: ocaml_${{ target_platform }} ${{ ocaml_compiler_version }}.* ${{ c_toolchain }}
                - ocaml-dune

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/ocaml/opam
  license: LGPL-2.1-only
  license_family: LGPL
  license_file: opam/LICENSE
  summary: Objective Caml (OCaml) is an implementation of the ML language.
  description: |
    opam is a source-based package manager. It supports multiple simultaneous compiler
    installations, flexible package constraints, and a Git-friendly development workflow.
  repository: https://github.com/ocaml/opam

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - dslarm
    - fasiha
    - MementoRC
